summary: Leadership built on a simple premise: research and design are only valuable when they change what gets built. Across seven years at Coupa Software, the UX organisation grew from six industrial designers with no shared process or tooling into a discipline of 40+ designers and researchers serving 20+ concurrent product lines inside a 5,000-person business. That growth was engineered rather than inherited. It came from founding the UX Research function single-handedly and then scaling it, from establishing the infrastructure that makes qualitative insight reusable (a governed Dovetail repository, standardized taxonomy, research intake, UEQ and UX KPI benchmarks), and from a long-term vision that deliberately staged research maturity from Micro (quick and dirty for important projects) through Meso (a process anyone can use to request research) and Macro (feature research shaping product roadmaps) to Mega (strategic UX research across all Coupa products, with demonstrated ROI). The underlying philosophy is drawn from a decade of academic research practice at Karolinska Institutet: outcome over output, flexibility over structure, moving teams from doubt to certainty with evidence, and making technology invisible. A software engineering background allows the same person to sit credibly with data scientists, engineers and product managers during early discovery, before anyone knows what to build.
